name: Act of August 7, 1882 providing for the sale of part of the Omaha reservation
promises: The land west of the Sioux City and Nebraska Railroad right of way would be sold only with the Omaha's consent expressed in open council, after appraisal by three commissioners, one selected by the tribe (section 1).
No land would be sold below its appraised value, and never for less than two dollars and fifty cents an acre (section 2).
Royce records that the rest of the reservation was to be allotted and patented to individuals or to the tribe.
today: In Nebraska v. Parker (No. 14-1406, March 22, 2016) the Supreme Court held that the 1882 Act did not diminish the Omaha Indian Reservation. A 1951 Commission petition by Omaha individuals refused allotments under the Act was dismissed because it raised individual, not tribal, claims (Docket 85).
